aesthetic.direction: modern System-Settings rounded-card utility with consumer warmth (badge-driven feedback)

psychology: Aesthetic-Usability Effect — polished rounded cards + green success checks make a lossy operation feel trustworthy
Immediate feedback / positive reinforcement (Doherty-adjacent) — the big blue NN% savings badge rewards each completed compression, a per-file dopamine hit
Von Restorff (isolation) — the single saturated blue badge pops against an otherwise monochrome row, aiming the eye at the payoff
Jakob's Law — settings reuse native macOS System-Settings conventions (pref tab bar, grouped cards, segmented controls) so users feel instantly at home
Hick's Law — settings chunked into labelled one-topic cards reduces choice overload
notes: Only evidence is cover.png, a marketing feature-grid composite; the app windows inside it are shown rotated ~5deg with slight perspective and downscaled, so ALL geometry is (estimated) with low confidence — accent HUES are reliable (scanned), pixel distances are not. No standalone gallery screenshots in source (meta.json shots: []). Accent binds to near-exact system Blue (#0080F8) and system Green (#30C840); green is correctly always glyph-paired. Native tells are strong (pref tab bar, native segmented/checkbox/switch, disabled-greyed settings minimize/zoom, 13pt-class density) despite the composite. Dark mode + Chinese localization exist (an occluded dark settings window is visible behind) but are not measurable. Icon.png was NOT digested (Workflow A / UI only, per task). Marketing copy claims 'Native Mac App' — visual evidence supports native SwiftUI, but no Liquid Glass material is present so era read as big-sur/sequoia, not liquid-glass.
